title: Spiking Neural Networks Are Harder to Steal: A Benchmark Study of Model Stealing Attacks
abstract: arXiv:2610.36298v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Machine learning models deployed behind query interfaces expose more than their predictions, because an adversary can use those predictions to rebuild the model itself. Model stealing attacks (MSAs) exploit this exposure by training a surrogate model that replicates the decision behavior of a target through black-box queries alone, without access to its parameters or training data. These attacks are well characterized for conventional artificial neural networks (ANNs), yet spiking neural networks (SNNs) process information in a fundamentally different way. SNNs communicate through sparse, discrete spikes, and their outputs depend on membrane potentials that evolve over time rather than on a static mapping from input to output. This temporal mode of computation suggests that the decision behavior of an SNN may be harder to reconstruct from its responses. translated_title: 脉冲神经网络更难被窃取：模型窃取攻击的基准研究
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.36298v1 公告类型：new 摘要：部署在查询接口背后的机器学习模型所暴露的不仅仅是其预测结果，因为攻击者可以利用这些预测来重建模型本身。模型窃取攻击（MSAs）正是利用了这种暴露，仅通过黑盒查询训练一个替代模型来复制目标模型的决策行为，而无需访问其参数或训练数据。这类攻击在传统人工神经网络（ANNs）上已被充分研究，然而脉冲神经网络（SNNs）以一种根本不同的方式处理信息。SNNs通过稀疏、离散的脉冲进行通信，其输出依赖于随时间演化的膜电位，而非从输入到输出的静态映射。这种时间维度的计算模式表明，SNN的决策行为可能更难从其响应中重建。本工作通过对四种代表性的MSA进行基准测试来验证这一可能性，即……
tldr: 本研究通过基准测试四种代表性的模型窃取攻击，证明由于脉冲神经网络采用基于稀疏离散脉冲和时变膜电位的时间计算模式，其决策行为比传统人工神经网络更难通过黑盒查询被窃取重建。
en_tdlr: This benchmark study of four representative model stealing attacks demonstrates that spiking neural networks are harder to steal than conventional artificial neural networks, owing to their temporal computation based on sparse discrete spikes and time-evolving membrane potentials.
